title: Choose an Alternate Blue-Toned Visual World (Zero Climbing)
question: Re-rolled with zero rock-climbing motifs and a commitment to your blue palette and two flagship projects (StressAlpha & PokéBastion TD).

options.label: Prussian Cyanotype Engineering Blueprint
options.lineage: 1842 John Herschel Prussian-blue cyanotype architectural & mechanical plates
options.thesis: Deep Prussian-blue architectural blueprint plates with crisp cyan drafting callouts framing StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD as precision 50/50 system schematics.
options.viewport: Top architectural title block pinning Kevin Ding's credentials and scale gauges, above two 50/50 cyanotype specimen frames showcasing real StressAlpha & PokéBastion production screenshots with interactive sandbox toggles.
options.risk: Drafting lines must stay crisp and modern rather than feeling like an antique historical document.

raised.raise: Adopted strict monospace luminance alignment for all numerical readouts and coordinate scales.
Adopted stepped exposure test-strip tabs for switching cleanly between real production screenshots and interactive algorithm sandboxes.
Adopted numbered margin sequence columns (01–04) that trace system architecture from data ingestion to rendering.
Adopted dual-layer cyan/cobalt offset framing on active screenshot viewports so selected plates pop with physical depth.

options.label: Midnight Cinema & X-Ray Showcase
options.lineage: Amazon Prime Video X-Ray inspection overlays & Criterion Collection midnight blue screening rooms
options.thesis: A sleek midnight-blue streaming & engineering theater where StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD are presented as flagship releases with an interactive 'X-Ray Architecture' toggle.
options.viewport: Widescreen midnight-blue theater header above two 50/50 flagship release showcases (StressAlpha & PokéBastion TD) featuring real production screenshots and an 'X-Ray Mode' toggle that reveals the live DCF & A* engine.
options.risk: Familiar dark-mode media-platform grammar, though uniquely personal to a Prime Video engineer.

options.label: Abyssal Thermocline Telemetry
options.lineage: Mesophotic deep-ocean research submersibles & vertical depth-axis dive computers
options.thesis: An abyssal ink-blue interface ruled by a continuous vertical depth meter (0m → 400m) descending from flagship production apps into backend systems and off-hours logs.
options.viewport: A persistent left-hand vertical depth gauge in meters beside a 50/50 thermocline cyan showcase of StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD production captures.
options.case: Natively blue-drenched from surface cyan to abyssal navy, pairing monospace instrument digits with clean grotesk notes.
options.risk: Ocean depth markers (e.g. -120m) must remain subtle wayfinding rather than competing with software engineering facts.

options.label: Cobalt Tactical Command Deck
options.lineage: 90s anime command-center telemetry walls translated into high-contrast cobalt and ice cyan
options.thesis: A high-density tactical command deck with caliper leader lines, hexagonal grid telemetry, and monumental tabular counters framing your two flagship systems.
options.viewport: Command-deck status header with giant tabular counters over two framed tactical bays housing StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD screenshots and live sandboxes.
options.case: Bridges quantitative financial cockpits (StressAlpha) and tactical grid games (PokéBastion TD) into one unified HUD.
options.risk: Must restrain hazard borders so the real app screenshots remain the undisputed focal point.

options.label: Live ASCII Character Matrix
options.thesis: Single-ink phosphor monospace grid where glyph density renders light and structure.
options.viewport: A full-screen ASCII character matrix rendering project previews as selectable text.
options.case: ASCII glyph rendering obscures the crisp high-resolution screenshots of StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD.
options.kept: Strict monospace coordinate alignment for telemetry labels.
options.risk: Destroys the visual clarity of real production screenshots.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom Tray
options.thesis: Stepped exposure test strips emerging in chemical developer trays.
options.viewport: Sequential darkroom stations developing each project screenshot.
options.case: Analog photography darkroom conflicts with interactive financial modeling and browser game mechanics.
options.kept: Stepped test-strip tab selector for switching between production screenshots and interactive sandboxes.
options.risk: Slow chemical reveal metaphor feels sluggish for a zero-latency systems engineer.

options.label: Deployable Origami Crease Sequence
options.thesis: A numbered sequence of geometric crease diagrams unfolding across one sheet.
options.viewport: Centered square fold diagrams with numbered margin steps.
options.case: Origami folding metaphors have no connection to Kevin's software engineering or off-hours interests.
options.kept: Clean numbered margin sequence columns for organizing multi-layer tech stacks.

options.label: Two-Ink Risograph Zine
options.thesis: Halftone newsprint stock with deliberately misregistered overlapping spot inks.
options.viewport: Offset two-ink zine cover over a two-column project spread.
options.case: Misregistered print grain muddies fine UI screenshots and financial charts.
options.kept: Crisp dual-layer cyan/cobalt offset frame around active screenshot viewports.
options.risk: Halftone distortion hurts readability of dense financial tables.

canonCard.label: Midnight Navy Editorial Bento (Category Standard)
canonCard.thesis: Ultra-clean Vercel/Linear-inspired midnight-blue engineering portfolio with 50/50 flagship cards, zero metaphors, and crisp typography.
canonCard.viewport: Clean developer header with credentials and social links above a 50/50 split showcase of StressAlpha and PokéBastion TD with real screenshots and sandbox tabs.
canonCard.risk: No overarching metaphor—pure, high-craft modern software portfolio.
